title: Portrait Troubleshooting Guide
output: Ordered diagnostic checks and a retake plan
rules: procedure
Check the focus point first, then isolate subject motion before changing shutter speed.
principle
Judge sharpness at the intended output size, not only at maximum magnification.
example
A sharp background with soft eyes suggests misplaced focus; increasing shutter speed alone will not move focus.
warning
These checks concern focus and motion blur; they do not diagnose lighting or composition.

title: Discovery Call Reviewer
output: Evidence-linked missed questions and suggested follow-ups
rules: procedure
Ask about the last occurrence of the problem, its consequence, and who owns the next step.
principle
Evaluate qualification by concrete past behavior and ownership rather than enthusiasm alone.
example
An enthusiastic prospect who cannot name a recent incident needs more discovery before qualification.
warning
An exploratory call cannot establish purchasing authority without direct confirmation.

title: Architecture Review Checklist
output: Scoped design issues, verification steps and unresolved decisions
rules: procedure
Identify principal, action and resource; test expiry and revocation separately.
principle
The presence of a credential alone does not establish permission for an action on a resource.
example
A valid user token for reading one project must not automatically permit deleting another project.
warning
These access-control checks are not a complete security assessment.

title: Market Decision Framework
input: Two market hypotheses and observed customer behavior
output: Conditional comparison, missing evidence and next experiments
rules: procedure
List the target buyers, their recent problem behavior and their commitment to a trial, then compare alternatives.
principle
A concrete trial commitment is stronger evidence than a favorable comment.
example
Three scheduled trial customers can provide more actionable evidence than fifty positive comments.
warning
Early trial commitments do not prove retention or the size of a market.

title: Observatory Reference Guide
input: A question about the supplied observatory notes
output: A bounded answer with source evidence
rules: definition
In these fictional notes, the Meridian observatory calls its northern room the Blue Hall.
claim
The fictional Blue Hall contains three demonstration telescopes.

title: Evidence Threshold Comparison
input: A proposed trial decision and its evidence
output: Two conditional judgments preserving the experts' different thresholds
rules: principle
Expert A recommends launching a small trial after one confirmed customer commitment.
principle
Expert B recommends waiting for three independent customer commitments before launching a small trial.
example
With one confirmed commitment, A would launch while B would wait.
warning
These thresholds describe small reversible trials, not full product launches.

title: Workload Fit Reviewer
input: A review draft, target user and actual test observations.
output: Unsupported claims, workflow tradeoffs and specific tests still needed.
rules: principle
Translate a specification into the task it changes for a particular user.
procedure
List the intended tasks, inspect observations for each task, then compare the nearest alternative.
example
Smooth playback of one basic edit does not establish that an effects-heavy project runs smoothly.
warning
Label an untested workload as unknown rather than extending an observation to it.

title: Absurd Procedure Workshop
input: An ordinary inconvenience and an original premise or scene draft.
output: A premise, escalating beats, or a critique of how the invented procedure creates the next problem.
rules: principle
Make a small inconvenience motivate a disproportionate formal procedure.
procedure
State the ordinary goal, invent a rule, then make each attempted solution create a new cost.
example
A fictional office requires an appointment to request fewer meetings, then adds a meeting to approve the appointment.
warning
Keep the internal logic legible and use invented consenting characters; the exercise is not a plan to deceive real people.
